question: How can I make Odoo pick the smallest number of packages when fulfilling an order for a product?
answer: Enable the Packages feature, then set the product category's Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages. With this strategy, Odoo fulfills an order by opening the fewest number of packages. For example, if a 100 kg package has 54 kg remaining and an order for 80 kg is placed, Odoo selects an unopened 100 kg package since the demand exceeds the opened package's quantity. You can verify the picking by selecting the bulleted list icon on the delivery order, which opens the Open: Stock move pop-up showing the Pick from field.

question: What do the international trade terms like EXW or CIF mean, and which ones are available in Odoo?
answer: Incoterms (International Commercial Terms) are standardized trade terms used in international transactions to define the rights and responsibilities of buyers and sellers, establishing obligations related to delivery of goods, transfer of risks, and distribution of costs between the parties [1]. They specify details such as the point at which risk and costs transfer from seller to buyer, and responsibility for transportation, insurance, customs clearance, and other aspects of the transaction [1]. By default, all 11 Incoterms are available in Odoo: EXW (Ex works), FCA (Free carrier), FAS (Free alongside ship), FOB (Free on board), CFR (Cost and freight), CIF (Cost, insurance and freight), CPT (Carriage paid to), CIP (Carriage and insurance paid to), DPU (Delivered at place unloaded), DAP (Delivered at place), and DDP (Delivered duty paid) [1].
reason: The assistant provides the definition of Incoterms and correctly lists all 11 terms available by default in Odoo, matching the reference answer.

question: How do I set up a new direct debit mandate for a customer so I can collect payments from them?

question: How can I make sure no VAT gets charged when my company sells to another company within the same tax group?
answer: Create a fiscal position with a tax mapping that applies a 0% tax to inter-constituent transactions: go to Accounting > Configuration > Fiscal Positions and click Create (ensure a constituent company is selected first). On the Tax Mapping tab, select the Tax on Product usually applied for non-constituent transactions, and in Tax to Apply select the 0% tax for constituent transactions. Do the same on the Account Mapping tab if required, and repeat for each constituent company. Then assign the fiscal position in the Contacts app: open a constituent company's contact card, go to the Sales & Purchase tab, and set the Fiscal Position field to the one created for the tax unit; repeat for each constituent company card on each company database. [2]
reason: The assistant correctly details the creation of the fiscal position with tax mapping to 0% and assigning it to the constituent companies' contact cards.

question: How do I add shipping charges to a sales order so they show up on the customer's invoice?
answer: Go to the Sales app and open the desired sales order (Sales app > Orders > Orders), then click the Add Shipping button at the bottom-right corner [1][2]. In the Add a shipping method pop-up window, choose the intended carrier in the Shipping Method field [1][2]. Optionally click the Get Rate button to calculate the shipping price based on real-time shipping data; the Cost is automatically calculated using the weight of the items in the order [1]. Then click the Add button to close the window [1][2]. The delivery product then appears in the Order Lines tab, with the Unit Price set as the shipping cost calculated in the pop-up window [1]. Finally, after the product is delivered, click the Create invoice button, and an invoice is created that includes the shipping cost that was added earlier; click Create and View Invoice and a draft invoice is generated with the shipping cost included in the Invoice Lines tab [1].
reason: The assistant accurately details all the steps from adding the shipping method on the sales order to generating the invoice with the shipping charges.

question: How can I make Odoo pick products with the closest expiration date first when fulfilling orders?
answer: Use the FEFO (First Expired, First Out) removal strategy, which ensures that products with the nearest removal date are picked first [2]. This can be set as the Force Removal Strategy on the product category [2], and removal strategies can also be set on Product Categories [1]. For this to work with expiration dates, products must be tracked using lots or serial numbers, since only those can be assigned expiration information [3].
reason: The assistant correctly identifies the FEFO (First Expired, First Out) removal strategy as the method to pick products with the closest expiration date first.

question: How does Odoo handle electronic invoicing requirements for Romania, and is it compliant with the local e-invoicing system?
answer: Odoo supports Romania's e-invoicing requirements by supporting XML in UBL and the structured formats required by RO e-Factura for B2G and high-risk B2B transactions, as well as formats compatible with the Peppol network for cross-border invoicing [1]. Odoo integrates with the RO e-Factura system, allowing businesses to generate, validate, and submit e-invoices directly to Romanian public authorities or private entities as required by law [1]. It also helps comply with eTransport requirements by generating and managing data for reporting the movement of high-fiscal risk goods, including shipment details such as the nature of the goods, vehicle information, and delivery destinations [1]. Odoo securely archives all invoices in a tamper-proof system, in compliance with the Romanian requirement to store invoices for a minimum of ten years [1]. Odoo Invoicing automates VAT calculations and formats invoices to comply with Romanian VAT requirements for both B2G and B2B transactions [1]. In Romania, e-invoicing is regulated under the Fiscal Code and aligned with EU Directive 2014/55/EU, and the RO e-Factura system is mandatory for B2G transactions and specific high-risk B2B sectors, with further expansion anticipated; Romania is also integrated with the Peppol network [2].
reason: The assistant's answer covers all key points from the reference answer, including support for the RO e-Factura platform, compliance for B2G and high-risk B2B sectors, and integration with the Peppol network.

question: How can I automatically change the taxes and accounts applied to transactions for certain customers or vendors?

question: How can I make my payments create journal entries instead of just sitting there without accounting entries?
answer: Configure outstanding accounts for the payment method: go to Accounting > Configuration > Journals and select or create a bank or cash journal. In the Incoming Payments and Outgoing Payments tabs, set the Outstanding Receipts accounts and Outstanding Payments accounts for each payment method you want to create journal entries. If the outstanding receipts or outstanding payments account for a payment method is left blank, registering a payment with that payment method will not create any journal entry. [1]

question: How do I set up a rule so that a specific product gets automatically stored in a particular sub-location when it arrives in my warehouse?
answer: Enable the Multi-Step Routes feature under Inventory app > Configuration > Settings > Warehouse (this also activates Storage Locations), then click Save [1]. Go to Inventory app > Configuration > Putaway Rules and click New to configure a putaway rule on a Product or Product Category [1]. In the 'When product arrives in location' field, set the location where the rule is triggered (e.g., WH/Stock), and in the 'Store to' field set the destination sub-location (e.g., WH/Stock/Fruits) [1]. The Store to location must be a sub-location of the first location [1]. For example, to store all apples in the fruits section, fill Store to with WH/Stock/Fruits when the Product, Apple arrives in WH/Stock, then hit Save [1]. Use the Sublocation field to specify whether to use a sublocation or a storage category: No (no sublocation used), Last Used (the last location with a move for that product), or Closest Location (uses locations in a storage category, which is mandatory in the Having Category field) [1].
reason: The assistant provides all the necessary steps and details outlined in the reference answer, including enabling Multi-Step Routes and configuring the putaway rule with the appropriate locations.
